options.text: ₹1,23,414 crore; the excess provisions were retained as a buffer
₹1,76,051 crore; realised equity stood at 6.8% of the balance sheet, above the chosen 5.5% level
₹1,76,051 crore; realised equity had fallen below 5.5%, so provisions were released

solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹1,76,051 crore; realised equity stood at 6.8% of the balance sheet, above the chosen 5.5% level

I only
I, II and III

solution.explanation: A soiled note includes a two-piece note pasted together with both pieces of the same note and no essential feature missing (I). solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

'Mutilated banknote' is a banknote, of which a portion is missing, or which is composed of more than two pieces. 'Imperfect banknote' means any banknote, which is wholly or partially, obliterated, shrunk, washed, altered or indecipherable but does not include a mutilated banknote

50 per cent
100 per cent
0 per cent

solution.explanation: Coins and banknotes immediately available to meet obligations, CRR balances (required and excess) and claims on RBI with residual maturity under six months get a zero RSF factor: they need no stable funding.

options.text: 30 calendar days
Three months
One year
Five years

solution.why_others_wrong: 30 days is the LCR horizon; three months and five years are not used.
solution.final_answer: Option C: One year

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank under liquidity stress, having used all its other HQLA, draws funds under the Facility to Avail Liquidity for LCR (FALLCR). On what terms is this facility available?

options.text: At 200 bps above the LAF repo rate, availed or rolled over for up to 90 days
At the repo rate itself, for up to 14 days
At the Bank Rate, for up to one year
At 100 bps above the SDF rate, for up to 30 days

solution.explanation: FALLCR is available only under stress and after all other HQLA (including MSF-eligible securities) are used, with a declaration to that effect. It can be availed or rolled over for a maximum of 90 days, the securities attract MSF haircuts, and the rate is 200 bps above the prevailing LAF repo rate.
steps: Only in stress, after exhausting other HQLA
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options give tenors and rates that RBI has not prescribed for FALLCR.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bond in a bank's stock of HQLA is downgraded and ceases to be an eligible liquid asset. Under RBI's LCR rules, what may the bank do?

options.text: Keep it in the stock of HQLA for an additional 30 calendar days to adjust or replace it
Keep it in the stock until it matures
Remove it from the stock on the same day
Keep it for 90 days with RBI's prior approval

solution.concept: Grace period after loss of eligibility
solution.explanation: RBI allows a bank to keep an asset that becomes ineligible (for example, after a downgrade) in its stock of liquid assets for an additional 30 calendar days, so that it has time to adjust its stock or replace the asset.
steps: Asset becomes ineligible → 30 more calendar days in the stock
solution.why_others_wrong: There is neither an immediate removal rule nor a 90-day or till-maturity allowance.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Keep it in the stock of HQLA for an additional 30 calendar days to adjust or replace it

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

options.text: 95 per cent
90 per cent
50 per cent
100 per cent

solution.explanation: Stable retail and SBC deposits (non-maturity or under one year) get a 95% ASF factor and less stable ones 90%. Short-term funding from non-financial corporates gets 50%, and capital and liabilities of one year or more get 100%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 95% is for stable deposits; 50% for non-financial corporate funding under one year; 100% for capital and long-term liabilities.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 90 per cent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: For the LCR, 'stable' retail deposits are insured deposits held in transactional or relationship accounts. When is an account treated as 'transactional'?

options.text: When the depositor has made at least one transaction in the last 30 days
When the account is a current account of any business entity
When the depositor's salary or pension is credited automatically, or bills are regularly paid from it under a registered mandate
When the depositor uses a debit card on it

solution.explanation: RBI treats an account as transactional if the depositor's salary or pension is automatically deposited into it, or bill payments are regularly withdrawn from it through a registered mandate (ECS/NACH, utilities, loan repayments). A 'relationship' exists when, for instance, the depositor also holds another deposit, a locker, demat or loan account.
solution.why_others_wrong: A single recent transaction, debit card use or being a business current account does not meet RBI's test.
solution.final_answer: Option C: When the depositor's salary or pension is credited automatically, or bills are regularly paid from it under a registered mandate

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI requires banks to monitor the LCR in each 'significant' currency. When is a currency considered significant for this purpose?

When it forms 25% or more of the bank's HQLA
When the bank has a branch in a country using that currency
When the bank's aggregate liabilities in that currency are 5% or more of its total liabilities

solution.explanation: To capture currency mismatches, banks monitor the LCR in each significant currency, and a currency is significant if the aggregate liabilities denominated in it amount to 5% or more of the bank's total liabilities. steps: Liabilities in a currency ≥ 5% of total liabilities → significant currency → monitor its LCR

solution.final_answer: Option D: When the bank's aggregate liabilities in that currency are 5% or more of its total liabilities

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Over the next 30 days a bank expects cash outflows of ₹1,000 crore and contractual inflows of ₹900 crore. Its stock of HQLA is ₹300 crore. What is its LCR under RBI's rules?

solution.explanation: Inflows can be recognised only up to 75% of outflows: min(900, 750) = 750. Net cash outflows = 1,000 − 750 = 250. LCR = 300 ÷ 250 = 120%, above the 100% minimum. Without the cap the ratio would wrongly appear as 300 ÷ 100 = 300%.

solution.final_answer: Option C: 120%

Both may launch it without any further step, since each already has an approval
P may launch it freely, but Q must seek fresh approval because its approval was channel-specific

Tap and Pay UPI payments on NFC-enabled point-of-sale machines
UPI payments above ₹1 lakh to hospitals
UPI collect requests from merchants

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026, which also governs UPI AutoPay, what must the issuer's post-transaction notification include at the minimum, besides the merchant's name, amount, date and time and reference numbers?

The customer's credit score and available balance
The merchant's GSTIN and PAN
A one-time password to confirm the debit

Prior approval of the merchant
Nothing; it can be changed by the merchant on the customer's request
AFA validation by the issuer

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: From 1 August 2025, NPCI moved the execution of UPI AutoPay mandate debits to non-peak hours. Which periods does NPCI define as peak hours?

9 am to 12 noon and 4 pm to 8 pm
12 noon to 3 pm and 7 pm to 11 pm
10 am to 1 pm and 5 pm to 9:30 pm

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Neha's UPI Lite balance is ₹1,700. Under RBI's current limits for UPI Lite, (a) what is the most she can add right now, and (b) after topping up fully, what is the minimum number of UPI Lite payments needed to pay ₹4,600 to a merchant entirely from UPI Lite?

solution.explanation: The UPI Lite balance cannot exceed ₹5,000 at any time, so she can add at most ₹5,000 − ₹1,700 = ₹3,300 (online, with AFA). Each UPI Lite payment is capped at ₹1,000, so ₹4,600 needs at least ⌈4,600 ÷ 1,000⌉ = 5 payments.

solution.final_answer: Option B: (a) ₹3,300; (b) 5

The biller must send a paper bill to the customer
The customer must visit an agent outlet
NPCI must approve each payment

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How does RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025) describe the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS)?

A non-bank wallet system regulated as a prepaid payment instrument
A bank-led model for interoperable financial inclusion transactions at micro-ATM terminals through Business Correspondents, using Aadhaar authentication
A system for bulk credit of salaries operated by UIDAI

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

The beneficiary bank must reverse the transaction within T + 1 day, with ₹100 per day of delay beyond that
NPCI must credit the beneficiary from its own funds within T + 3 days
No time limit applies, as APBS payments are government transfers

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

II only

I, II and III

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which kinds of deposits may a payments bank accept under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025?

options.text: Savings, current and fixed deposits up to ₹2 lakh
Only fixed deposits of up to one year
Recurring deposits only
Only demand deposits, i.e. current and savings deposits

Funds transfer to another bank
Applying for and receiving a loan
Bill payments from the account

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A company has fund-based and non-fund-based facilities of ₹12 crore from the banking system and wants a current account with a payments bank. Under the current account rules in RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025 (as updated), what can the payments bank offer?

options.text: A normal current account without restriction
Only a collection account, whose credits must be remitted within two working days to the designated cash credit, overdraft or current account
Nothing, as payments banks cannot open current accounts
A current account, provided the balance stays below ₹2 lakh

solution.explanation: A bank may maintain a current account without restriction only where the banking system's aggregate exposure to the customer is below ₹10 crore. At ₹10 crore or more, only a collection account is allowed; funds credited must be remitted within two working days to the designated CC/OD/current account (after statutory dues and dues to the bank). ₹12 crore ≥ ₹10 crore, so only a collection account.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹12 crore exceeds the threshold; payments banks can open current accounts; the ₹2 lakh cap concerns individuals.

Nothing until the next half-yearly review
Convert the account into a savings account within a week
Notify the customer by 10 December 2026 that the account must be converted to a collection account or closed, and complete this by 10 February 2027

questions.question_text: Which statement on voting rights and share acquisition applies to small finance banks under the SFB Licensing Guidelines, 2025?

Voting rights are capped at 10%, and acquiring 1% needs RBI's approval

After the fifth year from the date of issue, on the dates on which interest is payable

On the simple average of the closing price of 999-purity gold for the previous three business days, as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA)
On the issue price plus accrued interest

solution.final_answer: Option B: The spread on fresh business (about 290 bps) was wider than on outstanding business (about 241 bps), and MCLR fell by 6 bps

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's Commercial Banks – Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA) Framework Directions, 2026:
I. They were finalised on 7 October 2026 after a draft of 7 August 2026.
II. Eligible banks may choose a simpler approach to the CVA capital charge.
III. They took effect immediately on issue.
Which of the above is/are correct?

options.text: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III

solution.explanation: CVA risk is the risk of loss from changes in the counterparty credit spread on derivatives. The draft of 7 August 2026 was finalised on 7 October 2026 with revisions such as letting eligible banks choose a simpler approach, more risk-sensitive supervisory risk weights and clearer recognition of CVA hedges. The Directions come into effect on 1 April 2027, so III is wrong.
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with III is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

questions.question_text:
In June 2026 RBI gave temporary relief to attract fresh non-resident deposits. By amendments of August–September 2026, the end date of these measures was advanced from 30 September 2026 to 31 August 2026. Consider:
I. Fresh FCNR(B) deposits of 3–5 years and NRE term deposits of 3 years or more were exempt from CRR and SLR.
II. The interest rate ceiling on fresh FCNR(B) deposits of 3–5 years was temporarily withdrawn.
III. The relief covered NRE savings deposits of any tenor.
Which of the above is/are correct?

options.text: II and III only
I and II only
I and III only
I, II and III

solution.explanation: I is correct: fresh FCNR(B) deposits of 3–5 years (from 8 June) and NRE term deposits of 3 years or more (from 19 June) were exempted from CRR/SLR, and advances against them were excluded from ANBC. II is correct: the interest ceiling on such FCNR(B) deposits was temporarily withdrawn. All these ended on 31 August 2026 instead of 30 September. III is wrong: only NRE term deposits of 3 years or more were covered.
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing III is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only
